content.text: Now the ghostty icon. The taskbar resolves icons from the `Papirus` icon theme by window class. Ghostty's class is `com.mitchellh.ghostty` — let me see whether that icon actually resolves.

input.command:
echo "=== waybar version ==="; waybar --version 2>/dev/null | head -1
echo; echo "=== ghostty desktop file ==="; find /usr/share/applications ~/.local/share/applications /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications -iname '*ghostty*' 2>/dev/null
echo; echo "=== Icon= line ==="; grep -h '^Icon=' $(find /usr/share/applications ~/.local/share/applications -iname '*ghostty*' 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null
echo; echo "=== ghostty icon files on disk ==="; find /usr/share/icons /usr/share/pixmaps ~/.local/share/icons -iname '*ghostty*' 2>/dev/null | head -20
echo; echo "=== does Papirus have ghostty? ==="; find /usr/share/icons/Papirus* -iname '*ghostty*' 2>/dev/null | head -5 || echo "(no Papirus match)"
echo; echo "=== comparison: chrome + code in Papirus ==="; find /usr/share/icons/Papirus -iname 'google-chrome.*' -o -iname 'code.*' 2>/dev/null | head -4

content.content:
=== man waybar-hyprland-workspaces: relevant opts ===
       shown only if visible.

       persistent-only:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If set to true, only persistent workspaces will be shown on bar.

       all-outputs:
            typeof: bool
            default: false
            If  set  to  false workspaces group will be shown only in assigned
       output. Otherwise, all workspace groups are shown.

       active-only:
--
           dispatcher instead of `workspace` in Hyprland.

       ignore-workspaces:
            typeof: array
            default: []
            Regexes to match against workspaces names. If there's a match, the
       workspace will not be shown. This takes precedence  over  show-special,
       all-outputs, and active-only.

       sort-by:
            typeof: string
            default: "default"
            If set to number, workspaces will sort by number.
           If  set  to name, workspaces will sort by name. If set to id, work‐
--
       •   active: Will be shown, when workspace is active
       •   special: Will be shown on non-active special workspaces
       •   empty:  Will  be  shown on non-active, non-special empty persistent
           workspaces
       •   visible: Will be shown on workspaces that are visible but  not  ac‐
           tive.  For  example:  this is useful if you want your visible work‐
           spaces on other monitors to have the same look as active.
       •   persistent: Will be shown on non-empty persistent workspaces

EXAMPLES
           "hyprland/workspaces": {
                "format": "{name}: {icon}",
                "format-icons": {
                     "1": "",
--
                     "default": ""
                },
                "persistent-workspaces": {
                     "*": 5, // 5 workspaces by default on every monitor
                     "HDMI-A-1": 3 // but only three on HDMI-A-1
                }
           }

           "hyprland/workspaces": {
--
                     "default": ""
                },
                "persistent-workspaces": {
                     "*": [ 2,3,4,5 ], // 2-5 on every monitor
                     "HDMI-A-1": [ 1 ] // but only workspace 1 on HDMI-A-1

lastPrompt: Why do I have an extra workspace with nothing inside of it on my waybar taskbar?

content.text:
I have both answers. Let me lay out what I found before asking how you want them fixed.

**The empty workspace is workspace 4, and it lives on your laptop's built-in screen.**

`hyprctl workspaces` shows four workspaces: 1, 2, and 3 on `HDMI-A-1` (with 1, 4, and 1 windows), plus workspace 4 on `eDP-1` with **zero windows**. Hyprland guarantees every connected monitor always has exactly one active workspace, and it will not destroy that workspace even when it's empty — so as long as your laptop panel is on, workspace 4 exists. Your `hyprland.lua:238` only disables `eDP-1` on lid close, and the lid is currently open.

What makes it *visible* is `config.jsonc:29`, `"all-outputs": true`, which tells waybar to render workspaces from every monitor on every bar. So the bar on your external monitor faithfully shows the laptop screen's empty workspace. Nothing is broken — it's two settings behaving as documented.

**Ghostty has no icon because it's a snap, and waybar can't see snap `.desktop` files.**

This one has a false lead worth naming: Papirus *does* ship `com.mitchellh.ghostty.svg` (I found it at six sizes). So "the icon is missing from the theme" is wrong, and installing another icon theme would not help.

The actual break is one step earlier, in the window-class → app lookup. Waybar needs to map the window class `com.mitchellh.ghostty` to an app entry, and the only file declaring `StartupWMClass=com.mitchellh.ghostty` is `/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/ghostty_ghostty.desktop`. Reading waybar's live environment from `/proc/213808/environ`, **`XDG_DATA_DIRS` is not set at all** — and `/etc/profile.d/snapd.sh`, the script that normally appends snapd's directory, doesn't exist on this machine. With the variable unset, GLib falls back to the spec default `/usr/local/share:/usr/share`, which is exactly why `code` and `google-chrome` resolve (their desktop files sit in `/usr/share/applications`) while every snap silently fails.

I should be straight about one limit: I haven't read waybar 0.14's source to confirm it *only* uses the desktop-entry path and never tries the raw class as an icon name. But since Papirus has the icon and it still doesn't render, the desktop-entry path is where it's failing either way, so making that file reachable is the fix regardless.

Both fixes have a real choice in them, and the second has a trap — since `XDG_DATA_DIRS` is currently *unset*, setting it must re-include `/usr/local/share:/usr/share` explicitly, or Chrome and VS Code lose their icons.

questions.question: Workspace 4 is the active (empty) workspace on your laptop panel eDP-1. How do you want to get rid of it?

options.label: Bar shows own monitor only
options.description: Set "all-outputs": false in config.jsonc:29. Each monitor's bar lists only its own workspaces, so the external bar shows 1/2/3 and the laptop bar shows 4. Keeps the laptop screen fully usable. Reversible one-line change.

options.label: Turn off laptop screen
options.description: Add a permanent `hl.monitor({ output = "eDP-1", disabled = true })` to hyprland.lua. Workspace 4 stops existing entirely, on every bar. Only right if you never use the built-in panel while docked.
options.preview:
-- hyprland.lua, MONITORS section
hl.monitor({
    output   = "eDP-1",
    disabled = true,
})

-- hyprctl workspaces → 1, 2, 3 only
-- (lid-switch binds at L238/243
--  become redundant)

options.label: Hide workspace 4 by name
options.description: Add "ignore-workspaces": ["4"] to the workspaces module. Per the man page this takes precedence over all-outputs. Brittle: hides any workspace that happens to be numbered 4, and breaks if the laptop's workspace gets a different id.

questions.question: Ghostty's snap .desktop file is invisible because XDG_DATA_DIRS is unset. How broadly should I fix it?

options.label: Fix all snaps via XDG_DATA_DIRS
options.description: Set XDG_DATA_DIRS in hyprland.lua's ENV section to include snapd's dir plus the two defaults that are currently implicit. Fixes the icon for every snap you ever install, not just ghostty. Requires a Hyprland restart.
options.preview:
-- hyprland.lua, ENV section (~L67)
hl.env("XDG_DATA_DIRS",
  "/var/lib/snapd/desktop:" ..
  "/usr/local/share:/usr/share")

-- the two defaults MUST be listed:
-- the var is currently UNSET, so
-- omitting them breaks chrome+code

options.label: Fix only ghostty
options.description: Copy the snap's desktop file into ~/.local/share/applications/ (already searched, since XDG_DATA_HOME is set). Narrow and needs no Hyprland restart, but every future snap hits the same bug.
options.preview:
cp /var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/ \
     ghostty_ghostty.desktop \
   ~/.local/share/applications/

# StartupWMClass=com.mitchellh.ghostty
# Icon=/snap/ghostty/current/...png
# both already correct in the file

options.label: Both
options.description: Set XDG_DATA_DIRS as the general fix, and also drop the desktop file in ~/.local/share/applications as a belt-and-braces measure that works before the next Hyprland restart.
options.preview:
1. hl.env("XDG_DATA_DIRS", ...)
     → durable, all snaps

2. cp ghostty_ghostty.desktop
     ~/.local/share/applications/
     → takes effect immediately

Verify: restart waybar, icon appears

# Waybar: pin workspaces 1–9, and fix the missing ghostty icon

## Context

Two unrelated symptoms on the same bar, both now diagnosed.

**1. "An extra workspace with nothing inside."** `hyprctl workspaces` reports workspaces
1/2/3 on `HDMI-A-1` and workspace **4 on `eDP-1` with zero windows**. Hyprland always keeps
exactly one active workspace alive per connected monitor and never destroys it, even when
empty — so while the laptop panel is on, workspace 4 exists. `config.jsonc:29` sets
`"all-outputs": true`, so the external monitor's bar renders it. Nothing is broken.

The real want, per the user: **a stable row of workspaces 1–9**, always present, rather than
buttons that appear and vanish as workspaces get created and destroyed. That is
`persistent-workspaces`.

**2. Ghostty has no taskbar icon.** A tempting false lead: Papirus *does* ship
`com.mitchellh.ghostty.svg` (six sizes under `/usr/share/icons/Papirus/*/apps/`), so the icon
theme is *not* the problem and swapping themes would not help. The failure is one step
earlier, in the window-class → app lookup. The only file declaring
`StartupWMClass=com.mitchellh.ghostty` is the snap's exported entry at
`/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/ghostty_ghostty.desktop`. Reading waybar's live
environment (`/proc/<waybar-pid>/environ`) shows **`XDG_DATA_DIRS` is not set at all**, and
`/etc/profile.d/snapd.sh` — the script that normally appends snapd's directory — does not
exist on this machine. With the variable unset, GLib falls back to the spec default
`/usr/local/share:/usr/share`, which is exactly why `code` and `google-chrome` resolve (their
desktop files live in `/usr/share/applications`) while **every snap silently fails**.

Intended outcome: a fixed 1–9 workspace row, and ghostty (plus any future snap) showing its
icon.

## Decisions taken

- Pin **1–9**. Accepted caveat: `SUPER+0` → workspace 10 (`conf/keybinds.lua:105`) remains
  bound, so a transient 10th button will still appear when workspace 10 holds a window. The
  `SUPER+0` binds are left alone.
- Fix ghostty **both** ways: the durable env var, plus a local desktop-file copy that takes
  effect without a full session restart.

## Verified facts this plan relies on

- Waybar **v0.14.0**.
- `createWorkspace()` in `src/modules/hyprland/workspaces.cpp` dedups by workspace id
  (`w->id() == workspaceId`). The `"*"` key applies per-monitor, but the second monitor's pass
  finds the existing id and only updates persistence flags. So `"*": [1..9]` with
  `all-outputs: true` yields **9 buttons, not 18**. `all-outputs` can stay `true`.
- `style.css` has no base `#workspaces button` rule — only
  `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` (`style.css:30`) and `#workspaces.taskbar button`.
  Inactive workspaces already render as plain numbers, so six more need **no new assets and no
  CSS change**.
- `ghostty_ghostty.desktop` already contains a correct absolute
  `Icon=/snap/ghostty/current/share/icons/hicolor/512x512/apps/com.mitchellh.ghostty.png`

# Convert waybar `image` modules to CSS `background-image`

## Context

The waybar config uses four native `image` modules (`image#clock`, `image#network`,
`image#bluetooth`, `image#battery`) to render pokemon sprites. Waybar's `image` module
sizes via a single `size:` value that acts as a **bounding box**, not a height. Because
the sprites have different aspect ratios, the rendered heights don't match:

| Module | Sprite | Intrinsic size | Aspect | `size:` | Rendered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image#clock` | `dialga.png` | 800×800 | 1:1 | 32 | 32×32 |
...

# Waybar: pin workspaces 1–9, and fix the missing ghostty icon

## Context

Two unrelated symptoms on the same bar, both now diagnosed.

**1. "An extra workspace with nothing inside."** `hyprctl workspaces` reports workspaces
1/2/3 on `HDMI-A-1` and workspace **4 on `eDP-1` with zero windows**. Hyprland always keeps
exactly one active workspace alive per connected monitor and never destroys it, even when
empty — so while the laptop panel is on, workspace 4 exists. `config.jsonc:29` sets
`"all-outputs": true`, so the external monitor's bar renders it. Nothing is broken.

The real want, per the user: **a stable row of workspaces 1–9**, always present, rather than
buttons that appear and vanish as workspaces get created and destroyed. That is
`persistent-workspaces`.

**2. Ghostty has no taskbar icon.** A tempting false lead: Papirus *does* ship
`com.mitchellh.ghostty.svg` (six sizes under `/usr/share/icons/Papirus/*/apps/`), so the icon

content.text:
Both fixed and verified on screen. Your bar now reads `1 2 ⬤ 4 5 6 7 8 9` — nine buttons, pokeball on the active one — and ghostty renders its icon next to Chrome in the taskbar.

**The empty workspace was never a bug.** Hyprland keeps exactly one active workspace alive per connected monitor and refuses to destroy it even when empty, so your laptop panel `eDP-1` always held one. `"all-outputs": true` in `config.jsonc:29` meant the external monitor's bar dutifully drew it. Pinning 1–9 via `persistent-workspaces` makes that irrelevant: the row is now fixed, so whichever workspace the laptop happens to own is just one of the nine. (You can see it in that last check — `eDP-1` currently owns workspaces 1 and 4, and the bar doesn't flinch.)

The nine-vs-eighteen question resolved the way waybar's source predicted: `"*"` is applied per monitor, but `createWorkspace()` dedups on workspace id, so the second monitor's pass only updates flags. Nine buttons, `all-outputs` left alone.

**Ghostty was a snap-visibility problem, not an icon-theme problem.** Papirus had `com.mitchellh.ghostty.svg` the whole time — that's exactly the ghost-with-`>_` you now see. What was missing was the `.desktop` file declaring `StartupWMClass=com.mitchellh.ghostty`, which snapd exports only to `/var/lib/snapd/desktop`, a directory absent from `XDG_DATA_DIRS`. The variable is unset entirely on this machine, and `/etc/profile.d/snapd.sh` doesn't exist to add it, so GLib fell back to `/usr/local/share:/usr/share` — which is why Chrome and VS Code always worked and every snap silently didn't.

Worth being precise about what's proven, since it affects what you should expect after a reboot. The last check shows waybar's pid never changed and `XDG_DATA_DIRS` is *still* unset in its environment — so the `hl.env` line in `hyprland.lua` has not taken effect yet. The icon appearing right now is entirely due to the desktop-file copy into `~/.local/share/applications`, found via `XDG_DATA_HOME`. That's a clean result: it confirms the diagnosis and proves change #3 stands on its own. The `hyprland.lua` change is the durable one that will cover future snaps, and it stays untested until you next log in — worth a glance at `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(pgrep -x waybar)/environ | grep XDG_DATA_DIRS` after that.

Two things I left alone, per the plan:

- `SUPER+0` still jumps to workspace **10** (`conf/keybinds.lua:105`), which isn't pinned. When it holds a window you'll see a transient tenth button appear and vanish — the same behavior that prompted your original question. Say the word and I'll either pin ten or drop those three binds.
- The missing `/etc/profile.d/snapd.sh` is odd for a snapd install and suggests your `start-hyprland` session never sources login-shell profile scripts. Not causing trouble beyond this, but it's the root reason, and it could bite other snap integrations.

Your bar now reads `1 2 ⬤ 4 5 6 7 8 9` — nine buttons, pokeball on the active one — and ghostty renders its icon next to Chrome in the taskbar.

**The empty workspace was never a bug.** Hyprland keeps exactly one active workspace alive per connected monitor and refuses to destroy it even when empty, so your laptop panel `eDP-1` always held one. `"all-outputs": true` in `config.jsonc:29` meant the external monitor's bar dutifully drew it. Pinning 1–9 via `persistent-workspaces` makes that irrelevant: the row is now fixed, so whichever workspace the laptop happens to own is just one of the nine. (You can see it in that last check — `eDP-1` currently owns workspaces 1 and 4, and the bar doesn't flinch.)

The nine-vs-eighteen question resolved the way waybar's source predicted: `"*"` is applied per monitor, but `createWorkspace()` dedups on workspace id, so the second monitor's pass only updates flags. Nine buttons, `all-outputs` left alone.

**Ghostty was a snap-visibility problem, not an icon-theme problem.** Papirus had `com.mitchellh.ghostty.svg` the whole time — that's exactly the ghost-with-`>_` you now see. What was missing was the `.desktop` file declaring `StartupWMClass=com.mitchellh.ghostty`, which snapd exports only to `/var/lib/snapd/desktop`, a directory absent from `XDG_DATA_DIRS`. The variable is unset entirely on this machine, and `/etc/profile.d/snapd.sh` doesn't exist to add it, so GLib fell back to `/usr/local/share:/usr/share` — which is why Chrome and VS Code always worked and every snap silently didn't.

Worth being precise about what's proven, since it affects what you should expect after a reboot. The last check shows waybar's pid never changed and `XDG_DATA_DIRS` is *still* unset in its environment — so the `hl.env` line in `hyprland.lua` has not taken effect yet. The icon appearing right now is entirely due to the desktop-file copy into `~/.local/share/applications`, found via `XDG_DATA_HOME`. That's a clean result: it confirms the diagnosis and proves change #3 stands on its own. The `hyprland.lua` change is the durable one that will cover future snaps, and it stays untested until you next log in — worth a glance at `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(pgrep -x waybar)/environ | grep XDG_DATA_DIRS` after that.

Two things I left alone, per the plan:

- `SUPER+0` still jumps to workspace **10** (`conf/keybinds.lua:105`), which isn't pinned. When it holds a window you'll see a transient tenth button appear and vanish — the same behavior that prompted your original question. Say the word and I'll either pin ten or drop those three binds.
- The missing `/etc/profile.d/snapd.sh` is odd for a snapd install and suggests your `start-hyprland` session never sources login-shell profile scripts. Not causing trouble beyond this, but it's the root reason, and it could bite other snap integrations.","background_tasks":[],"session_crons":[]}

That's a different bug from the two we fixed — the taskbar module is showing stale window icons for an empty workspace. Let me reproduce it and look, rather than theorize.

I'll switch to an empty workspace, screenshot, and immediately switch back.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/27e5adf4-38d1-4d69-b186-ce735765fe5b/scratchpad
ORIG=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id); echo "original active ws: $ORIG"
GEO=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="HDMI-A-1")|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"')

grim -g "$GEO" before.png
hyprctl dispatch workspace 6 >/dev/null
grim -g "$GEO" empty6.png
echo "ws6 windows per hyprland: $(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .windows)"
hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null
echo "restored to $ORIG"

command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick || M=convert
$M empty6.png -crop 700x56+1050+0 +repage -scale 200% empty6-zoom.png
$M before.png -crop 700x56+1050+0 +repage -scale 200% before-zoom.png
echo done

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Probe: does the #taskbar module show stale windows on an empty workspace?
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
OUT=probe.log; : > "$OUT"
log(){ echo "$*" >> "$OUT"; }

geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r --arg m "$1" '.[]|select(.name==$m)|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
state(){
  log "  focused monitor : $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.focused)|.name')"
  log "  activeworkspace : $(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r '"id=\(.id) windows=\(.windows)"')"
  log "  per-monitor act : $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -rc '[.[]|{(.name):.activeWorkspace.id}]')"
  log "  live workspaces : $(hyprctl workspaces -j | jq -rc '[.[]|{id:.id,mon:.monitor,win:.windows}]')"
}

ORIG=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)
ORIGMON=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.focused)|.name')
log "=== ORIGINAL (ws $ORIG on $ORIGMON) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_before_hdmi.png
grim -g "$(geo eDP-1)"    p_before_edp.png

# focus HDMI-A-1 first so the empty workspace lands on the monitor we watch
hyprctl dispatch focusmonitor HDMI-A-1 >/dev/null; sleep 1
log ""; log "=== FOCUSED HDMI-A-1 ==="; state

hyprctl dispatch workspace 6 >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
log ""; log "=== AFTER dispatch workspace 6 (should be EMPTY) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_ws6_hdmi.png
grim -g "$(geo eDP-1)"    p_ws6_edp.png

hyprctl dispatch workspace 7 >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
log ""; log "=== AFTER dispatch workspace 7 (also EMPTY) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_ws7_hdmi.png

hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null; sleep 0.5
hyprctl dispatch focusmonitor "$ORIGMON" >/dev/null; sleep 0.5
hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null
log ""; log "=== RESTORED ==="; state

M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
for f in p_ws6_hdmi p_ws7_hdmi p_before_hdmi; do
  $M $f.png -crop 760x56+1020+0 +repage -scale 200% ${f}_zoom.png
done
echo DONE >> "$OUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Probe: does the #taskbar module show stale windows on an empty workspace?
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
OUT=probe.log; : > "$OUT"
log(){ echo "$*" >> "$OUT"; }

geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r --arg m "$1" '.[]|select(.name==$m)|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
state(){
  log "  focused monitor : $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.focused)|.name')"
  log "  activeworkspace : $(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r '"id=\(.id) windows=\(.windows)"')"
  log "  per-monitor act : $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -rc '[.[]|{(.name):.activeWorkspace.id}]')"
  log "  live workspaces : $(hyprctl workspaces -j | jq -rc '[.[]|{id:.id,mon:.monitor,win:.windows}]')"
}

ORIG=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)
ORIGMON=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.focused)|.name')
log "=== ORIGINAL (ws $ORIG on $ORIGMON) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_before_hdmi.png
grim -g "$(geo eDP-1)"    p_before_edp.png

# focus HDMI-A-1 first so the empty workspace lands on the monitor we watch
hyprctl dispatch focusmonitor HDMI-A-1 >/dev/null; sleep 1
log ""; log "=== FOCUSED HDMI-A-1 ==="; state

hyprctl dispatch workspace 6 >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
log ""; log "=== AFTER dispatch workspace 6 (should be EMPTY) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_ws6_hdmi.png
grim -g "$(geo eDP-1)"    p_ws6_edp.png

hyprctl dispatch workspace 7 >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
log ""; log "=== AFTER dispatch workspace 7 (also EMPTY) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_ws7_hdmi.png

hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null; sleep 0.5
hyprctl dispatch focusmonitor "$ORIGMON" >/dev/null; sleep 0.5
hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null
log ""; log "=== RESTORED ==="; state

M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
for f in p_ws6_hdmi p_ws7_hdmi p_before_hdmi; do
  $M $f.png -crop 760x56+1020+0 +repage -scale 200% ${f}_zoom.png
done
echo DONE >> "$OUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Probe: does the #taskbar module show stale windows on an empty workspace?
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
OUT=probe.log; : > "$OUT"
log(){ echo "$*" >> "$OUT"; }

geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r --arg m "$1" '.[]|select(.name==$m)|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
state(){
  log "  focused monitor : $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.focused)|.name')"
  log "  activeworkspace : $(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r '"id=\(.id) windows=\(.windows)"')"
  log "  per-monitor act : $(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -rc '[.[]|{(.name):.activeWorkspace.id}]')"
  log "  live workspaces : $(hyprctl workspaces -j | jq -rc '[.[]|{id:.id,mon:.monitor,win:.windows}]')"
}

ORIG=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)
ORIGMON=$(hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.focused)|.name')
log "=== ORIGINAL (ws $ORIG on $ORIGMON) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_before_hdmi.png
grim -g "$(geo eDP-1)"    p_before_edp.png

# focus HDMI-A-1 first so the empty workspace lands on the monitor we watch
hyprctl dispatch focusmonitor HDMI-A-1 >/dev/null; sleep 1
log ""; log "=== FOCUSED HDMI-A-1 ==="; state

hyprctl dispatch workspace 6 >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
log ""; log "=== AFTER dispatch workspace 6 (should be EMPTY) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_ws6_hdmi.png
grim -g "$(geo eDP-1)"    p_ws6_edp.png

hyprctl dispatch workspace 7 >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
log ""; log "=== AFTER dispatch workspace 7 (also EMPTY) ==="; state
grim -g "$(geo HDMI-A-1)" p_ws7_hdmi.png

hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null; sleep 0.5
hyprctl dispatch focusmonitor "$ORIGMON" >/dev/null; sleep 0.5
hyprctl dispatch workspace "$ORIG" >/dev/null
log ""; log "=== RESTORED ==="; state

M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
for f in p_ws6_hdmi p_ws7_hdmi p_before_hdmi; do
  $M $f.png -crop 760x56+1020+0 +repage -scale 200% ${f}_zoom.png
done
echo DONE >> "$OUT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

content.text:
No leak — two bars, two script instances each with its `while` subshell and `socat`. That's the expected count.

Now the burst test: switch from a full workspace to an empty one and capture at 150 ms, 400 ms, 1 s, and 2.5 s to see whether icons linger and then clear.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/27e5adf4-38d1-4d69-b186-ce735765fe5b/scratchpad
: > burst.log
ws(){ hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = $1 })" >/dev/null; }
geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="HDMI-A-1")|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
ORIG=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)
echo "orig=$ORIG" >> burst.log

hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 2 })" >/dev/null; sleep 2
grim -g "$(geo)" b_t0_ws2.png
echo "on ws2: windows=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .windows)" >> burst.log

ws 5
for d in 0.15 0.4 1.0 2.5; do
  sleep "$d"
  grim -g "$(geo)" "b_ws5_$d.png"
  echo "t=$d active=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r '"\(.id)/win\(.windows)"')" >> burst.log
done

ws "$ORIG"; sleep 0.3
echo "restored=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)" >> burst.log

M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
for f in b_t0_ws2 b_ws5_0.15 b_ws5_0.4 b_ws5_1.0 b_ws5_2.5; do
  $M "$f.png" -crop 760x56+1020+0 +repage -scale 200% "${f}_z.png"
done
# stitch the four post-switch frames into one strip, labelled
$M b_ws5_0.15_z.png b_ws5_0.4_z.png b_ws5_1.0_z.png b_ws5_2.5_z.png -append burst_strip.png

content.text:
Still stale at 400 ms — the pokeball has settled on 5, yet the taskbar shows workspace 2's windows. So this isn't an animation frame; the window list genuinely lags behind.

My 1 s and 2.5 s samples were contaminated (something moved focus back to 3 mid-test — possibly you). Let me measure the real clearing latency, recording the active workspace with every frame so I can discard contaminated samples.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/27e5adf4-38d1-4d69-b186-ce735765fe5b/scratchpad
: > lat.log
geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="HDMI-A-1")|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
G=$(geo)
ORIG=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)

hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 2 })" >/dev/null; sleep 2
hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 5 })" >/dev/null
START=$(date +%s.%N)
for i in $(seq 1 14); do
  grim -g "$G" "l_$i.png"
  A=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)
  T=$(echo "$(date +%s.%N) - $START" | bc)
  printf "frame %2d  t=%.2fs  active=%s\n" "$i" "$T" "$A" >> lat.log
  sleep 0.25
done
hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = $ORIG })" >/dev/null

# "has icons" = count distinct colours in the icon strip (icons are colourful; empty bar is flat)
M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
echo "--- icon-strip colour count per frame (high = icons present) ---" >> lat.log
for i in $(seq 1 14); do
  C=$($M "l_$i.png" -crop 200x40+1380+8 +repage -format %k info:)
  printf "frame %2d  colours=%s\n" "$i" "$C" >> lat.log
done
echo LATDONE >> lat.log
cat lat.log

(3) Is there anything that only refreshes visibility on window events (openwindow/closewindow/movewindow) rather than workspace-change events? (4) How does the empty/persistent workspace interact with active-only visibility?

lastPrompt: I am toggling between the workspaces but the workspaces with nothing are getting showned with whatever tabs in the workspaces before.

content.text:
Four seconds, workspace 5 active and empty, and the bar still shows workspace 2's four windows. Confirmed persistent.

Here's the part that matters for the fix, and it reframes things. **Two independent modules are stale at once**, while a third updates correctly:

- `hyprland/workspaces` (the numbers) — **correct**, pokeball moved to 5.
- `hyprland/workspaces#taskbar` (the icons) — **stale**, still showing workspace 2.
- `custom/taskbar-divider` (the `│`) — **stale**, still drawn, even though `workspace-tabs.sh` exists precisely to hide it when the active workspace is empty.

Those last two are wholly separate mechanisms — one is native C++ in waybar, the other is your bash script with its own `socat` listener on Hyprland's event socket. They have no reason to fail together for the same internal reason. That they're both stuck, while the module right next to them updates fine, says the trigger is something they share: both key off *the active workspace of a specific monitor* (`all-outputs: false` for the taskbar, `WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME` for the script), whereas the numbers module uses `all-outputs: true` and just follows global focus.

Two things undercut a tidy story, and I'd rather flag them than paper over them:

- My earlier 3→6 test came out **clean** — same shape, empty destination, both modules correct. So "switch to an empty workspace" alone doesn't trigger it. Something about the 2→5 path does, and I haven't isolated what.
- I fetched waybar's source and the summary claims `active-only` is *parsed but never used*, with visibility driven by `getVisibleWorkspaces()` instead. That would be a genuine upstream bug and fits your symptom — but it came from a summarizer, not my own reading of the code, and I don't trust it enough to act on.

I've spent a fair amount of the session on this probing already (the cost hooks are shouting), so I want to check before I burn more.

Also, housekeeping: my tests moved you across workspaces 2, 5, 6, and 7 and restored you to 3 each time. If your window focus feels shuffled, that's me, not the bug.

content.text:
Now I have the plumbing clear: `isPersistent()` is true only from `persistent-workspaces` config or Hyprland rules, and the **taskbar module has neither** — so active-only *should* hide the old workspace there. My reading says persistence can't explain the taskbar staleness, yet the bug appeared right after I added persistent-workspaces. When source-reading and the timeline disagree, I test.

Decisive experiment: reproduce 2→5 with persistent-workspaces temporarily removed. If it clears, my change is implicated despite the theory; if it stays stale, persistence is a red herring. I'll also capture what the divider script emits directly. This briefly reloads your bar and flicks workspaces.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/27e5adf4-38d1-4d69-b186-ce735765fe5b/scratchpad
: > matrix.log
CFG=~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc
cp "$CFG" cfg.backup
geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="HDMI-A-1")|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
ws(){ hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = $1 })" >/dev/null; }
reload(){ killall -SIGUSR2 waybar; sleep 1.5; }
repro(){  # $1 = tag
  ws 2; sleep 1.5
  ws 5; sleep 1.5
  grim -g "$(geo)" "m_$1.png"
  # what the divider script reports for HDMI right now:
  local dv; dv=$(WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME=HDMI-A-1 bash ~/.config/waybar/scripts/workspace-tabs.sh 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  echo "$1: active=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id) dividerScriptSaysActiveHasWindows=$dv" >> matrix.log
}

echo "=== A: WITH persistent-workspaces (current) ===" >> matrix.log
reload; repro A_withpersist

echo "=== B: WITHOUT persistent-workspaces ===" >> matrix.log
python3 - "$CFG" <<'PY'
import sys,re
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
s=re.sub(r'\n\s*//[^\n]*persistent-workspaces[^\n]*','',s)  # drop the comment lines
s=re.sub(r'\n\s*"persistent-workspaces":[^\n]*\n', '\n', s)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
grep -q persistent-workspaces "$CFG" && echo "  (still present!)" >> matrix.log || echo "  (removed ok)" >> matrix.log
reload; repro B_nopersist

echo "=== restore original config ===" >> matrix.log
cp cfg.backup "$CFG"; reload
ws 3; sleep 0.3
echo "restored active=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j | jq -r .id)" >> matrix.log

M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
for t in A_withpersist B_nopersist; do
  $M "m_$t.png" -crop 800x56+1000+0 +repage -scale 200% "m_${t}_z.png"
done
$M m_A_withpersist_z.png m_B_nopersist_z.png -append matrix_cmp.png
echo MATRIXDONE >> matrix.log
cat matrix.log

lastPrompt: I am toggling between the workspaces but the workspaces with nothing are getting showned with whatever tabs in the workspaces before.

content.text:
That's the likely mechanism. Reading `update()` (workspace.cpp:195): when active-only hides a workspace, it does `m_button.hide(); return;` at line 208 — **returning before `updateTaskbar()` is ever called** (line 249). So a hidden workspace's icons are never cleared, only hidden. For them to still be *visible*, ws2's button isn't being hidden at all — meaning waybar still considers ws2 active on that monitor, even though `updateWorkspaceStates()` re-reads state on every event. That's either a race (consistent with 3→6 being clean but 2→5 stale) or an upstream active-only bug.

First, let me clean up — my reloads leaked 9 copies of the divider script, and the test left you on empty workspace 5. Full waybar restart resets it.

content.text: Found the real problem: my `pkill -f 'workspace-tabs.sh'` pattern matches the harness's own shell wrapper (which echoes my command containing that string), so it kills its own shell every time — that's the recurring exit 1. Let me kill the orphans via a Python script that reads `/proc` and skips its own process tree.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import os, signal
me = os.getpid(); parent = os.getppid()
mine = {me, parent, os.getpgid(0)}
killed = []
for pid in [int(p) for p in os.listdir('/proc') if p.isdigit()]:
    if pid in mine: continue
    try:
        cl = open(f'/proc/{pid}/cmdline','rb').read().replace(b'\0',b' ').decode('utf-8','replace')
        comm = open(f'/proc/{pid}/comm').read().strip()
    except Exception:
        continue

lastPrompt: I am toggling between the workspaces but the workspaces with nothing are getting showned with whatever tabs in the workspaces before.

content.text:
Your bar is back up and rendering correctly — workspaces 1–9 with the pokeball on the active workspace 3, the divider, and workspace 3's two window icons (Chrome + ghostty). waybar is a single clean instance, config intact, and you're on a real workspace. Sorry for the flicker during that stretch — my process cleanup matched the harness's own shell wrapper and I had to chase it down.

Here's where the investigation actually landed.

**The bug is real and reproducible.** Switching from a populated workspace (2, four windows) to an empty one (5), the taskbar keeps showing the old workspace's icons — and it *never* clears, still stale 4 seconds later. So this isn't a repaint lag; it's a genuine state bug. Your description was exactly right.

**The earlier "active-only isn't implemented" claim was wrong.** I downloaded waybar 0.14.0's actual source and read it. `active-only` *is* implemented (`workspace.cpp:201`): a workspace's button hides when it's `!active && !persistent && !visible && !special`. The summary I'd relied on was mistaken — good thing we didn't act on it.

**The mechanism, as far as I got:** when active-only hides a workspace, it calls `m_button.hide()` and returns *before* clearing the taskbar's window icons (`workspace.cpp:208` returns above the `updateTaskbar()` call at line 249). So for the old icons to remain *visible*, that button isn't being hidden at all — which means waybar still believes the old workspace is active on that monitor, even though `updateWorkspaceStates()` re-reads Hyprland on every event. That points to a **race**, and the evidence fits: my first test (3→6) came out clean, while 2→5 is reliably stale. Same shape, different result — nondeterministic.

**What I did not finish:** the controlled matrix test (with/without persistent-workspaces) hung — on *my* bug, not yours: the divider script runs an infinite `socat` loop, and I captured it under `$(...)` which blocks forever. So I still can't say for certain whether the persistent-workspaces change I made *triggers* this or merely coincided with you noticing it. My source reading says the taskbar module has no persistent config and shouldn't be affected — but reading and the timeline disagree, which is exactly the case where I don't want to hand-wave.

I've spent a lot of budget here (the cost hooks are flashing), so I want your call rather than burning more unprompted.

content.text: The gap right of the pill is pure black (`srgb(0,0,0)`), while the pill is teal `srgb(0,76,106)`. That's a clean detector: measure mean brightness of a fixed band just right of where the empty pill ends — near-zero when the taskbar is correctly empty, elevated when stale (pill+icons extend into it). Let me calibrate the band with a known-empty and known-stale frame.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/27e5adf4-38d1-4d69-b186-ce735765fe5b/scratchpad
M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="HDMI-A-1")|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
G=$(geo)
band(){ $M "$1" -crop 200x36+1430+10 +repage -colorspace Gray -format '%[fx:mean*255]' info:; }

# REF_STALE: reproduce it (2 populated -> 5 empty), capture
hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 2 })" >/dev/null; sleep 1.3
hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 5 })" >/dev/null; sleep 1.3
grim -g "$G" ref_after_switch.png
echo "after 2->5 switch: active=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j|jq -r .id) bandMeanGray=$(band ref_after_switch.png)"

# REF_CLEAN: while sitting on empty 5, force a fresh full reload -> correct empty render
killall -SIGUSR2 waybar; sleep 1.6
grim -g "$G" ref_reload_empty.png
echo "empty 5 after reload:   active=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j|jq -r .id) bandMeanGray=$(band ref_reload_empty.png)"

# REF_POPULATED: switch to 2 (populated), capture
hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 2 })" >/dev/null; sleep 1.3
grim -g "$G" ref_populated.png
echo "populated 2:            active=$(hyprctl activeworkspace -j|jq -r .id) bandMeanGray=$(band ref_populated.png)"
hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = 3 })" >/dev/null
input.description: Calibrate detection band with stale, clean, populated frames

lastPrompt: I am toggling between the workspaces but the workspaces with nothing are getting showned with whatever tabs in the workspaces before.

content.text:
**Major finding.** All three frames — including "empty after a full reload" — show the *same* four icons (Chrome, two VS Code, ghostty), which are workspace 2's windows. That means:

1. The staleness **survives a complete waybar reload** (SIGUSR2). So this is **not a switch-time race** — it's deterministic. The taskbar is stuck showing a specific populated workspace's windows even when the active workspace (correctly marked by the pokeball on 5) is empty.
2. That flips my earlier race hypothesis. It's a logic bug in which workspace the `active-only` taskbar picks.

The remaining variable is persistent-workspaces. Since it's now reload-deterministic, I can test it cleanly. Let me test persist-OFF with a guaranteed config restore (trap), reloading while sitting on an empty workspace.

input.command:
cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/27e5adf4-38d1-4d69-b186-ce735765fe5b/scratchpad
M=convert; command -v magick >/dev/null && M=magick
CFG=~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc
cp "$CFG" cfg.safe.backup
restore(){ cp cfg.safe.backup "$CFG"; killall -SIGUSR2 waybar 2>/dev/null; }
trap restore EXIT
geo(){ hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[]|select(.name=="HDMI-A-1")|"\(.x),\(.y) \(.width)x56"'; }
G=$(geo)
ws(){ hyprctl dispatch "hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = $1 })" >/dev/null; }
crop(){ $M "$1" -crop 900x56+950+0 +repage -scale 150% -gravity North -background '#222' -splice 0x16 -fill yellow -pointsize 13 -annotate +8+2 "$2" "$3"; }

# --- persist ON: visit ws3 (populated), go ws6 (empty), reload, capture ---
ws 3; sleep 1; ws 6; sleep 1
killall -SIGUSR2 waybar; sleep 1.6
grim -g "$G" t_on_after3.png
crop t_on_after3.png "persistON reload@ws6empty (visited ws3)" c1.png

# --- persist OFF: remove the line, reload, visit ws3, go ws6, reload, capture ---
python3 - "$CFG" <<'PY'
import sys,re
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
s=re.sub(r'\n[^\n]*//[^\n]*dedups[^\n]*','',s)
s=re.sub(r'\n\s*"persistent-workspaces":[^\n]*','',s)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
echo "persist lines after strip: $(grep -c persistent-workspaces $CFG)"
killall -SIGUSR2 waybar; sleep 1.6
ws 3; sleep 1; ws 6; sleep 1
killall -SIGUSR2 waybar; sleep 1.6
grim -g "$G" t_off_after3.png
crop t_off_after3.png "persistOFF reload@ws6empty (visited ws3)" c2.png

$M c1.png c2.png -append persist_test.png
ws 3
echo "montage done"
input.description: Test staleness with persist on vs off, reload-based
